title: Finite-field internal Hom from a finite local system
statement: Let $A$ be a finite field and $S$ a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Use ordinary uncompleted derived categories of module sheaves over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal B_A(T)$ for the complexes whose cohomology [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] vanishes outside a finite interval and is constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: there is a finite constructible locally closed stratification on which each cohomology sheaf is pro-étale locally constant with finite-dimensional $A$-module values. Let $L$ be an $A_S$-module sheaf admitting a pro-étale covering on each member of which it is a constant finite-dimensional $A$-module [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. For integers $a\le b$ and $N\in\mathcal B_A(S)$ with $H^r(N)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, the ambient ringed-site $R\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(L[0],N)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] belongs to $\mathcal B_A(S)$ and has cohomology zero outside the same interval $[a,b]$. More precisely, with $L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(L,A_S)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], there are natural isomorphisms $H^rR\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(L,N)\cong L^\vee\otimes_{A_S}H^r(N)$ for all $r$, with sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13, local-system case of the finite-coefficient computation, using the ringed-site perfect-dual formula.

proof.text: Put $R=A_S$ and choose the given covering $\{U_i\to S\}$ with $L|_{U_i}\simeq\underline{V_i}$. A finite basis of $V_i$ identifies this with $R|_{U_i}^{\oplus d_i}$, where $d_i=\dim_A V_i\geq0$; sheafifying the basis maps and their inverse gives the identification. By the definition of sheaf Hom, $L^\vee|_{U_i}\simeq R|_{U_i}^{\oplus d_i}$. For any module sheaf $M$ define $e_M:L^\vee\otimes_R M\to\mathcal Hom_R(L,M)$ by $e_M(\lambda\otimes m)(x)=\lambda(x)m$. In this basis its inverse is $f\mapsto\sum_{j=1}^{d_i}e_j^\vee\otimes f(e_j)$, and both composites are identities by $x=\sum_j e_j^\vee(x)e_j$. Restriction to the slice of $U_i$ is the module inverse image along $U_i\to S$ by clause 3 of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], so by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] it commutes with the tensor product, and by the definition of sheaf Hom it commutes with $\mathcal Hom_R$; hence the restriction of $e_M$ to $U_i$ is the evaluation map formed from $L|_{U_i}$ and $M|_{U_i}$. Thus $e_M$ is locally invertible, and its local inverses agree on overlaps because each inverts the same map; the sheaf gluing axiom gives a global inverse. These maps are natural contravariantly in $L$ and covariantly in $M$, since evaluation commutes with precomposition and postcomposition. The same calculation shows that $L^\vee$ is locally constant with finite-dimensional models. Empty sums give the assertions for $d_i=0$.

source.place: Tag 0FNY, example-dual: finite-free evaluation calculation; Section 03DH, section-localize, and Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact: exact slice restriction.

proof.text: The functor $T(M)=\mathcal Hom_R(L,M)$ is exact. Indeed restrict a short exact sequence of module sheaves to each $U_i$. Exact slice restriction is supplied by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and on this slice $T$ is the finite direct sum functor $M\mapsto M^{\oplus d_i}$ by the basis calculation of step 1, so the resulting sequence is exact. The kernel, middle homology and cokernel of its image under $T$ consequently restrict to zero. Their vanishing is detected by this covering, by clause 1 of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative]; [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] identifies its covering inverse images with the slice restrictions used here. This proves exactness globally, without assuming exactness of sections or conservativity of geometric-point stalks.

source.place: Tag 0FNY, example-dual: finite-free evaluation calculation; Section 03DH, section-localize, and Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact: exact slice restriction.

proof.text: Represent $N$ by a cochain complex $C^\bullet$, and use the K-injective resolution $C^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Since the first argument is $L[0]$, that definition represents $R\mathcal Hom_R(L,N)$ by the complex $T(I^\bullet)$, with differential $T(d_I)$: the Hom-complex differential has no source differential in this case. An exact additive functor preserves kernels, images and their quotient, so step 2 and [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] give $H^r(T(I^\bullet))\simeq T(H^r(I^\bullet))\simeq T(H^r(N))$. Apply $e_{H^r(N)}^{-1}$ from step 1 to obtain the asserted isomorphism $H^rR\mathcal Hom_R(L,N)\simeq L^\vee\otimes_R H^r(N)$. Kernel and image comparisons are functorial, and evaluation is natural, so these are natural isomorphisms. This argument works for arbitrary $N$ in the uncompleted derived category.

source.place: Section section-internal-hom, K-injective construction of derived internal Hom; agent exact-functor cohomology calculation for a degree-zero locally free source.

proof.text: Choose a finite constructible locally closed stratification witnessing the constructibility of $H^r(N)$, as in [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], and let $i:Z\to S$ be any one of its strata. By that definition $i^*H^r(N)$ is locally constant with finite geometric stalks, so [lem-sf-proetale-lisse-finite-models] gives a pro-etale covering of $Z$ on whose members it is the constant sheaf of a finite $A$-module $W$; it is a finite-dimensional $A$-space. Step 1 gives finite locally constant models $A^{d_i}$ for $L^\vee$; [lem-exc-proetale-pullback-locally-constant] therefore gives such models for $i^*L^\vee$ on the base-changed covering, with the same finite-dimensional $A$-spaces. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor], $i^*(L^\vee\otimes_R H^r(N))\simeq i^*L^\vee\otimes_{A_Z}i^*H^r(N)$. Take the common pro-etale refinement by fibre products of the two trivializing coverings. Restricting along a member $V\to U$ of the refinement is the module inverse image by clause 3 of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], so constant models stay constant with the same module by [lem-exc-proetale-pullback-locally-constant], and the restriction of the tensor is the tensor of the restrictions by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. On $V$, choose a basis of the first model, of dimension $d$. Tensoring with its constant sheaf is then a direct sum of $d$ copies of the second constant sheaf, hence is the constant sheaf of $W^{\oplus d}$ if the second model is $W$. This value is finite-dimensional, and finite as a set since $A$ is finite. Thus $i^*(L^\vee\otimes_RH^r(N))$ has finite constant models on a pro-etale covering of $Z$, and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-model-stalks] shows that its geometric stalks are finite. So it is locally constant with finite geometric stalks on each of the original strata, and $L^\vee\otimes_RH^r(N)$ is constructible by the cited definition. This uses the given stratification, without a geometric finiteness or purity theorem.

source.place: Tag 093R, lemma-pullback-locally-constant; finite-free tensor calculation on common trivializing coverings; constructibility as in literature/stacks-project/proetale.tex, Tag 09AJ, definition-constructible.

proof.text: For $r\notin[a,b]$, $H^r(N)=0$, so the formula of step 3 gives $H^rR\mathcal Hom_R(L,N)=L^\vee\otimes_R0=0$. For the remaining finitely many degrees, step 4 proves constructibility. These two assertions are exactly membership in $\mathcal B_A(S)$ with the same cohomological interval. If $S$ is empty or $L=0$ the formula gives the zero object in every degree; if $a=b$, the argument gives a single cohomology sheaf in that degree.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13, local-system case; the sharper same-interval conclusion follows from the preceding explicit computation.

proof_origin.place: Finite-free local-basis argument of Tag 0FNY, exact restriction in Section 03DH and pullback of locally constant sheaves in Tag 093R, combined with the K-injective definition of derived internal Hom. Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 6.7.13 is context, not a claim of this precise same-interval statement under its general hypotheses.
